exposure: Bupivacaine infiltration directly in the rectus sheath
outcome: time of first demand for analgesia
cohort: 49 patients who underwent Lower Segment Cesarean Section (LSCS) at Apollo hospital, Belapur, Navi Mumbai.
finding: Bupivacaine infiltration directly in the rectus sheath post-cesarean section was found to be a safe, effective, and convenient method for postoperative analgesia, leading to good pain control and early mobilization with minimal side effects.
cross-section timing: Immediate postoperative period (data extracted from records up to 14 hours post-surgery)
